headline: High-risk shared-workflow pair: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution plus Airbyte’s broad egress create dangerous default paths for leakage, cascading errors, and compliance drift.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API calls, while Langflow can chain multiple agents and run server-side Python unsandboxed by default. If Langflow ingests Airbyte outputs through a shared flow or file handoff, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Langflow flow nodes pass Airbyte output into an LLM or tool node without provenance tagging
IF a shared file or server-side store is used as the bridge between Airbyte and Langflow
mitigations: Add a provenance label to every Airbyte output before Langflow consumes it
Insert a manual review step before any Langflow agent acts on Airbyte text
Restrict Langflow nodes to structured fields only, not raw content
Disable server-side Python code components for the shared flow
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Langflow reads and writes the server filesystem, stores per-flow credentials, and sends data to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services. In a shared deployment, Airbyte data can flow into Langflow and then out to third parties by default. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive business data.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs business data into a Langflow flow
IF Langflow components forward that data to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services
IF uploaded files or server-side state contain the same business data
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and Langflow on separate workspaces
Block Langflow flows from sending business data to external providers
Store secrets outside Langflow for the shared workflow
Use redaction before any Langflow API call
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and data-class policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs with broad egress, and Langflow can execute shell, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even though Airbyte itself does not request write access, the pair can still contend over shared files or downstream resources in a flow. Because Langflow’s server-side execution is unsandboxed by default, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same server filesystem or shared output directory
IF Langflow shell or Python components mutate artifacts that Airbyte also reads or publishes
mitigations: Separate writable directories for each agent
Disable shell and package-install steps in shared flows
Run Langflow with a locked-down service account
Avoid shared mutable git or file state
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow system that can chain multiple agents, while Airbyte produces data that downstream components may treat as input. If Langflow treats Airbyte output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into automated actions or further agent steps. The interaction is documented enough to see the pathway, but not enough to assume verification exists.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is fed into a Langflow node without validation
IF a downstream Langflow component sends emails, writes records, or triggers APIs based on that output
mitigations: Add schema validation between Airbyte and Langflow
Require human approval before any downstream action
Use a verification node that checks Airbyte outputs against source data
Limit Langflow to read-only summarization for this flow
requires-engineering: implement confidence gates and rollback for automated actions

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and can route data to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services. If regulated or residency-bound business data enters Langflow, retention and residency can diverge from Airbyte’s handling. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF business data subject to retention or residency rules is processed in Langflow
IF Langflow forwards that data to external model providers or HTTP services with different retention terms
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed in the shared flow
Set explicit retention limits for Langflow stores
Avoid sending regulated data to external providers
Review vendor terms for residency and retention
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
